title.value: The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned at the beginning of the paper.
title.quote: The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research

analysis.description: This paper introduces the BrowserGym ecosystem, which aims to standardize and enhance the research in web agents by providing a unified benchmarking platform for evaluating web agents. It expands the BrowserGym library to unify existing benchmarks and introduces AgentLab for agent creation and experimentation. The paper also includes empirical evaluations of state-of-the-art models to showcase the ecosystems' capabilities.

type.justification: The paper conducts empirical evaluations of web agents using various benchmarks to demonstrate the utility of BrowserGym and AgentLab.
type.quote: As a supporting evidence, we conduct the first large-scale, multi-benchmark web agent experiment and compare the performance of 6 state-of-the-art LLMs across 6 popular web agent benchmarks made available in BrowserGym.

name.justification: The research primarily focuses on benchmarking and tools for developing web agents.
name.quote: The BrowserGym ecosystem addresses the growing need for efficient evaluation and benchmarking of web agents, particularly those leveraging automation and Large Language Models (LLMs) for web interaction tasks.

name.justification: The paper introduces new benchmarks and integrates existing ones into a unified system.
name.quote: We propose an extended BrowserGym-based ecosystem for web agent research, which unifies existing benchmarks from the literature.

name.justification: The paper evaluates the performance of Large Language Models in the context of web agents.
name.quote: We compare the performance of six state-of-the-art LLMs / VLMs from the GPT-4 (OpenAI, 2024a), Claude 3.5 (Anthropic, 2024a) and Llama 3.1 families (Meta, 2024) across all web agent benchmarks available in BrowserGym.
